sources.title: Audi Q8 e-tron: More battery capacity and higher charging power (audi.com archive)
sources.notes: Q8 50: 89 kWh net / 95 gross, 150 kW DC; Q8 55 and SQ8: 106 net / 114 gross, 170 kW DC; nominal voltage 396 V. Market-neutral (Audi global).

sources.title: The most important facts about the new Audi Q8 e-tron (audi.com archive)
sources.notes: 396 V; 50: 89/95 kWh, 150 kW; 55 and SQ8: 106/114 kWh, 170 kW; AC 11 kW standard (Europe). No battery preconditioning described.

sources.title: Audi Q8 e-tron (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: Table: 2019 e-tron 55 95 kWh gross / 83.6 usable (later 86.5 after an Oct 2021 software update), 150 kW; Q8 55 and SQ8 114/106, 170 kW; US AC 9.6 kW charger supplied by Audi.

sources.title: Audi e-tron (2018) (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: 55 and SQ8 170 kW DC, 50 150 kW; US: a 40 A 9.6 kW J1772 charger is supplied by Audi; thermal system keeps battery at 23-35 C.

sources.title: Porsche And Audi EVs Can Use Tesla Superchargers, With One Exception (InsideEVs)
sources.notes: 2025-09-08: e-tron GT, Q6 e-tron and A6 e-tron gain Supercharger access; all other Audi/Porsche EVs compatible except Q4 e-tron; Canada same date; Audi EVs lack a NACS port so an adapter is needed; new 2025 Q6, A6 Sportback and e-tron GT include one; adapter sale to existing owners not announced.

sources.title: Audi and Porsche EV drivers gain NACS adapters (electrive)
sources.notes: Audi NACS DC adapter comes with new 2025 Q6 e-tron, A6 Sportback e-tron and e-tron GT; current owners do not yet have access to the adapter; quotes Audi: Q4 e-tron cannot currently use the adapter or the Tesla NACS Partner Supercharger network.

sources.title: What Charging Port Does the Audi Q8 e-tron (ChargePapa)
sources.notes: 2023-2024 Q8 e-tron: CCS1 inlet (J1772 AC, CCS1 DC); later years not named.

sources.title: Audi e-tron GT: Battery and thermal management (audi.com archive)
sources.notes: 84 kWh net / 93 gross, up to 270 kW at 800 V, 33 modules of 12 pouch cells, AC 11 kW standard (22 kW option announced), HPC destination in navigation intensifies battery cooling.

sources.title: Electromobility in winter: intelligent functions optimize range and charging performance (Audi, 2021-12-17)
sources.notes: e-tron GT quattro: route planner activates battery preconditioning while driving when a destination is set. Preconditioning not mentioned for e-tron 55, Q8 or Q4 in this release.

sources.title: Audi e-tron GT (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: Infobox: 93.4 kWh (84 kWh usable), 270 kW (800 V) DC, 11 kW AC.

sources.title: Audi e-tron GT refresh (InsideEVs)
sources.notes: 2025 e-tron GT: 105 kWh gross / 97 usable, 320 kW peak, 800 V, about 18 min 10-80 % under ideal conditions.

sources.title: Audi revises e-tron GT offer in the USA (electrive, 2024-11-26)
sources.notes: 2025 US e-tron GT (S and RS performance): 105 kWh battery on all models, 320 kW peak (up from 270), 10-80 % in about 18 min.

sources.title: Audi Q6 e-tron: Focus on charging performance (Audi press release)
sources.notes: 100 kWh gross / 94.9 net (12 modules), 270 kW DC max in series production, 800-volt system, AC 11 kW standard (Europe), "preconditioned HV battery" and predictive thermal management, 83 kWh variant to follow.

sources.title: Audi unveils 2025 Q6 e-tron and SQ6 e-tron (Cars.com)
sources.notes: US Q6: 94.9 kWh usable of 100 kWh, 270 kW DC, 9.6 kW onboard charger.

sources.title: Audi Q6 e-tron (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: 100 kWh pack "12-Modules NMC CATL", 94.9 kWh usable, 270 kW quattro, 260 kW 100 kWh Performance, 800-volt platform.

sources.title: Audi A6 e-tron (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: 100 kWh pack: twelve modules of prismatic NMC811 (CATL), 94.4 usable in text / 94.9 in table, 270 kW, 21 min 10-80 %, 800 V; onboard charger up to 11 kW Europe or 9.6 kW US; Canada quattro only.

sources.title: Audi unveils pricing and specs for 2025 Q6 e-tron featuring new range-leading RWD model (Electrek)
sources.notes: US RWD Q6 e-tron: 100 kWh battery, DC tops out at 260 kW (RWD), 270 kW lineup; 10-80 % in 21 min.

sources.title: 2025 A6 e-tron is Audi's longest-range BEV in the US (Wards)
sources.notes: A6 e-tron: 100 kWh gross (94.4 net), up to 270 kW on 800 V, 135 kW on 400 V, 10-80 % in 21 min.

sources.title: Audi releases new A6 and Q6 e-tron models in the USA (electrive, 2026-02-09)
sources.notes: 2027 US A6/S6 Sportback, Q6/SQ6 SUV and Sportback: all 100 kWh (94.4 net); RWD A6 e-tron single rear motor, rest quattro.

sources.title: The 2027 Audi Q6 and A6 e-tron have a power nap mode (InsideEVs)
sources.notes: 2027 A6/Q6 e-tron: 94.4 kWh pack, up to 270 kW, 10-80 % as little as 21 min. Port, AC and preconditioning not covered.

sources.title: Audi Q4 e-tron (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: Q4 40/45/50: 82 kWh gross / 77 usable; NMC cells (LG Energy Solution, CATL); AC 11 kW for 40 and up; DC 135 kW (2021 40/45/50) and 175 kW for 55 quattro pre-2026.

sources.title: 2024 Audi Q4 55 e-tron (InsideEVs)
sources.notes: US 2024 update: 82 kWh gross / 77 net, 175 kW (150 kW before), 10-80 % in 28 min, 11 kW onboard charger, route-planner DC charger prioritisation and battery preconditioning before charging "new for this model"; RWD Q4 40 dropped.

sources.title: 2025 Audi Q4 e-tron gets RWD variant back (Cars.com)
sources.notes: 2025 Q4 e-tron: 82 kWh, up to 175 kW, 10-80 % in 28 min (not trim-specific).

sources.title: Volkswagen e-Golf (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: 24.2 kWh (2014-16) and 35.8 kWh (2017); DC (CCS) max 40 kW; DC option also upgrades the onboard AC charger from 3.6 to 7.2 kW; 2017: 7.2 kW standard; DC optional on SE, standard on SEL Premium and Limited Edition.

sources.title: VW e-Golf (German Wikipedia)
sources.notes: Gross 24.2 (2014-17) / 35.8 kWh (2017-20); net 21.1-21.2 / 31.5 kWh; 323 V nominal (2014 model); CCS option 40 kW; 7.2 kW AC for the 2017 model.

sources.title: 2017 Volkswagen e-Golf ups range, power and price (Cars.com)
sources.notes: 35.8 kWh (from 24.2), 7.2 kW onboard charger newly standard, DC fast charging $995 option, standard on Limited Edition and SEL Premium; 80 % in about an hour.

sources.title: NACS DC adapter (vw.ca), e-Golf exclusion
sources.notes: Adapter officially for ID.4 and ID. Buzz; not compatible with the e-Golf.

sources.title: 2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz (vw.com)
sources.notes: 10-80 % in 26 minutes with 200 kW DC fast charging; 11 kW Level 2; Supercharger access with a Volkswagen-approved NACS DC adapter sold separately.

sources.title: Electric VW Bus for North America and Europe: world premiere of the ID. Buzz with long wheelbase (Volkswagen Newsroom)
sources.notes: 85 kWh net battery (long wheelbase); no gross figure on the page.

sources.title: Volkswagen ID. Buzz (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: Long wheelbase (North America): 91 kWh gross / 85 net, 11 kW AC; sold in US from June 2024 as MY2025.

sources.title: Audi e-tron under the skin: battery pack, motors and more (InsideEVs)
sources.notes: 95 kWh liquid-cooled pack (not labelled gross or net), nominal voltage 396 V, pouch cells 60 Ah from LG Chem, fast charging 150 kW (0-80 % in 30 min). 2018 launch material.

sources.title: Audi e-tron 95 kWh battery (The Weekly Driver)
sources.notes: Audi e-tron and Sportback 2019-2023: NCM 622, LG Chem/LGES pouch cells, 95 kWh total / 86.5 usable (83.6 on 2019 models); says the 2024 Q8 uses a different 114 kWh pack.

sources.title: Porsche J1 93.4 kWh battery (The Weekly Driver)
sources.notes: NMC, LG Energy Solution, 93.4 total / 83.7 usable; lists Audi e-tron GT 2022-2024.

sources.title: Porsche J1 105 kWh battery (The Weekly Driver)
sources.notes: NMC 811, LG Energy Solution, 105 total / 97 usable; lists Audi e-tron GT 2025-2026 (S and RS performance).

sources.title: Volkswagen e-Golf (EV Database NZ)
sources.notes: Battery type NMC, usable 32 kWh, 400 V architecture, DC 40 kW; used examples 2017-2021.

sources.title: 2025 Audi A6 Sportback e-tron prices in Canada (Auto123)
sources.notes: Canada: A6 Sportback e-tron quattro and Ultra e-tron quattro, dual-motor AWD 456 hp, 100 kWh (94.4 usable), up to 270 kW, 10-80 % in 21 min, AC up to 9.6 kW.

sources.title: Battery Passport proof-of-concept pilot 2 (Global Battery Alliance)
sources.notes: Audi battery: cell producer Samsung SDI (Hungary), chemistry NCA, total energy 114 kWh, 228 Ah, model "4P 115kWh".

sources.title: Volkswagen ID. Buzz LWB tech specs (EVSpecs)
sources.notes: ID. Buzz LWB: Lithium Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC), 91 kWh gross / 86 usable; US Pro S RWD listed.

ac_max_kw.notes: Cars.com (VW release): "Newly standard is a 7.2-kW onboard charger" (2017). 2018-2020 compared: no change shown. Canada not separately sourced.

charge_port.notes: Cars.com/Wikipedia: DC fast charging (CCS) $995 option on SE, standard on SEL Premium and Limited Edition. SE cars without the option have J1772 only (counts unknown). Canada not separately sourced.

supercharger_access.notes: VW Canada: the NACS DC adapter is officially for ID.4 and ID. Buzz and is not compatible with the e-Golf; Electrek (2025-11-12) lists only ID.4 and ID. Buzz. Applied to US and Canada.

battery.capacity_usable_kwh.notes: German Wikipedia: net 31.5 kWh per the registration table (2017-2020).

battery.chemistry.notes: Estimated: EV Database NZ lists the e-Golf (used examples 2017-2021) with battery type NMC, 32 kWh usable, 400 V, DC 40 kW. Community database, not a VW statement. The 24.2 kWh 2015-2016 pack is not covered by that page.

battery.capacity_usable_kwh.notes: VW Newsroom (LWB premiere): 85 kWh net battery. Wikipedia agrees (91 gross / 85 net).

battery.chemistry.notes: Estimated: EVSpecs lists the ID. Buzz long-wheelbase 91 kWh gross / 86 usable pack as Lithium Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC); the US 2025 car carries the same 91 kWh pack (Wikipedia, VW 85 net). Community database, not a VW statement.

battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: the ID. Buzz is built on VW's MEB platform, which Guide Auto lists at 400 V for the ID.4 82 kWh pack (the Buzz pack is larger, 91 kWh); no page states the Buzz voltage. Platform-level estimate.

battery.preconditioning.notes: Estimated: vw.com says that on "most 2024 and newer Volkswagen EV models" the car starts preheating the battery automatically when an active route to a DC fast charger is set (a Battery Optimization toggle exists in Charging Settings, which is not shown to be a manual start button). The page does not list models and the ID. Buzz is not named; the 2025 ID. Buzz is assumed included.

dc_max_kw.notes: vw.com: "Charge from 10% to 80% in 26 minutes with 200kw DC fast charging". Wikipedia gives 170 kW for the short-wheelbase pack only.

ac_max_kw.notes: vw.com: 11 kW Level 2 charger (240 V), up to about 9 hours from empty. Canada not separately sourced (same car).

published_10_80_min.notes: vw.com: 10-80 % in 26 minutes at 200 kW DC.

charge_port.notes: vw.com: a Volkswagen-approved NACS DC adapter is sold separately for Tesla Superchargers, so the car has a CCS1 DC inlet (VW Canada says the same).

supercharger_access.notes: VW Canada: NACS DC adapter officially available for ID.4 and ID. Buzz, unlocking Tesla NACS partner Superchargers across Canada and the US; Electrek 2025-11-12: access from 2025-11-18, $200 (CAD 304) adapter, MY2026+ include it.
